key_insight: ARGON speeds up neutral-atom quantum compilation by separating static spatial conflict resolution from dynamic temporal routing, using a GNN to pick layouts that avoid future transport bottlenecks.
engineering_relevance: This makes large-scale neutral-atom compilation more scalable and practical by reducing search complexity while preserving collision-free, high-parallelism execution.
method: Use a GNN to score candidate layouts against long-horizon temporal constraints
Apply a heuristic router to generate collision-free atom transport
evidence_signal: The abstract reports compilation in under 10 seconds, up to >10^4x and 600x average speedups over baselines, and up to 10^2x fidelity improvement on dense circuits.
watch_item: The approach depends on the quality of the precomputed layout library and GNN predictions, so robustness may vary when hardware conditions or circuit patterns shift beyond the training or certified set.
paper_title: ARGON: A GNN-Empowered Compilation Framework for Scalable Neutral Atom Computing
